title: Wegener to Modern Tectonics
welcome_lead: Trace theory from 1912 continental drift to modern plates.

walkthroughs.body_html: Coastline fit (S. America-Africa), Glossopteris fossil distribution across southern continents, glacial striations on tropical Africa, Permian coal in Antarctica. Lacking a mechanism, his theory rejected by geologists until 1960s.

Harry Hess (1962) proposed mid-ocean ridges produce new basaltic crust as mantle convects upward. Atlantic widens about 2.5 cm/yr. Vine-Matthews-Morley (1963) found symmetric magnetic stripes confirming hypothesis using paleomagnetism.

Seven major plates: Pacific, North American, Eurasian, African, Antarctic, Indo-Australian, South American. GPS measures plate velocities: Pacific moves NW at ~7 cm/yr relative to Eurasia. San Andreas Fault accommodates this transform motion in California.

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
The focus is at the centre of the Earth and the epicentre is on the surface.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Earthquakes are caused by magma rising up to the surface.
Earthquakes are caused by the Earth's core overheating.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
The sudden release of built-up stress along faults at plate boundaries as rocks slip past each other, generating seismic waves.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the focus and epicentre of an earthquake?
options: The focus (hypocentre) is the underground point where the earthquake originates; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus.
The focus is at the centre of the Earth and the epicentre is on the surface.
The focus and epicentre are the same point.
Earthquakes are caused by the Earth's core overheating.
